sections.theory:
v. Hit the ball twice

When the batsman, after hitting the ball or after stopping it with some part of his body, then deliberately hits the ball, he will be given out in case of hitting the ball twice. He can stop the ball with any part of the body except his bat or hands for the protection of his wickets.

vi. Hit wicket

If the batsman while playing the ball touches the wicket with the bat or some part of the body, he will be declared out. This is called “hit wicket out”. But if while making a run the bat or some part of the body touches the wicket, he will not be out.

vii. Leg before wicket

If the batsman stops the ball with some part of the body and the ball is exactly in line with the wickets — if he had not stopped it with some part of the body, he would have been bowled — the opposing player may appeal to the umpire and the umpire can declare him out.

viii. Run Out

After hitting the ball, the players run between the wickets to make runs. If before the player reaches his crease an opposing player touches the ball to the wickets, or throws it and it hits the wickets, then the player of that side becomes out.
